title: Pre-Analysis — Main Deck Hard Point Provisioning for Later Freighter Conversion, Frames 40 to 54
abstract: Original pre-analysis for the build-standard hard points and reinforced panel edges in the centre fuselage that let a later freighter conversion proceed without opening the floor grid, closed with three conditions.

sections.objective: Establish what the introduction of build-standard hard points and reinforced floor panel edges between frames 40 and 54 conflicts with, and confirm that the provisioning can be cut into production without a change to the passenger configuration that operators already fly. The work order had to identify the protective and drainage conditions the floor penetrations depend on, quantify the repair population at the intended fitting stations, and check what else is committed in the same two lower deck zones.
sections.findings_summary: The provisioning is straightforward as a design and awkward as a configuration item. The floor penetrations for the hard points rely on the drainage standard set at the forward door surround; on an aircraft without it the penetration sealing drains into a path that does not exist, which makes that standard a hard condition of embodiment rather than a recommendation. The panel edge insert repair is the second constraint: aircraft carrying an elongated insert at a fitting station have no sound material for the hard point and would need a local renewal first. The removal task for the floor panels is the working document for the conversion itself and today says nothing about hard points or their protection. The extended discharge suppression standard occupies the same two zones with a distribution manifold that runs under the panels being reinforced.
sections.next_steps: Declare the drainage standard as a post-mod condition in the applicability and state it in the retrofit bulletin. Add a pre-embodiment insert repair survey at the fitting stations and carry the result into the conversion downtime estimate. Raise a maintenance change request so the panel removal task identifies the hard points and their protection. Agree the manifold routing with fire protection before production cut-in rather than resolving it on the line.

similarity_seeds: hard points so a later conversion does not require the floor grid to be opened
reinforced floor panel edge at a restraint fitting station

tasks.title: Identify protection and drainage conditions on the floor penetrations
Quantify the insert repair population at the fitting stations
Check committed work in the same lower deck zones

evidence.similarity_note: No shared identifier and no shared vocabulary: one is a floor structure provisioning document, the other a protection and drainage standard at a door surround two sections forward. The link is the drainage path the penetration sealing assumes.

expected_findings.rationale: The hard point penetrations are sealed against a drain path that only exists on aircraft at the chromate-free protection standard. Without that standard the sealing drains into structure, which is exactly the condition the earlier work was raised to remove.
expected_findings.resolution: Declare the standard as a post-mod applicability condition and state it in the retrofit bulletin.

evidence.similarity_note: The same panel and insert set by entity link, and the two texts describe the same edge condition in nearly the same words.

expected_findings.rationale: An elongated insert repair at a fitting station leaves no sound material for the hard point. The provisioning assumes a pristine edge and the repair population at those stations is material on the older aircraft in the range.
expected_findings.resolution: Add a pre-embodiment insert repair survey and carry the result into the conversion downtime estimate.

expected_findings.rationale: The panel removal task is the working document for the conversion itself and says nothing about hard points, their protection or the order in which panels come off around them. Post-embodiment it would be followed on a floor it does not describe.
expected_findings.resolution: Raise a maintenance change request identifying the hard points and their protective treatment.

expected_findings.rationale: The rebalanced suppression distribution manifold runs under the panels being reinforced, in the same two zones. The reinforced edge changes the panel underside clearance at three stations and the routing has never been drawn against the new edge.
expected_findings.resolution: Agree the manifold routing with fire protection before production cut-in.

expected_non_findings.reason: Returned by every search over these two zones and shares the compartment context exactly. Its ground points and lighting run sit on the shell side of the bay, not under the floor panels, and no harness attaches to the panel edge the provisioning reinforces.

type_data.conclusion: The provisioning proceeds subject to the drainage standard condition, an insert repair survey and the manifold routing agreement.
